IUT3.Def1_1.content: Defines the tautological log-link from an F-prime-strip to its logarithm, the (full) log-link obtained by post-composing with a (full) poly-isomorphism, and log-shells: at nonarchimedean v the log-shell is (p_v^*)^{-1} times the pre-log-shell, where p_v^* = p_v for odd p_v and p_v^2 for p_v = 2; at archimedean v a corresponding construction via the pointed universal covering. Mono-analytic versions for F^{⊢×μ}- and D^⊢-prime-strips are given in (iv), (v).
explicit_hypotheses: initial Θ-data as in IUTchI Def 3.1
external_dependencies: AbsTopIII: Def 3.1 (iv), Def 5.4 (iii), Prop 3.2 (iii), Def 4.1 (iv), Prop 4.2, Prop 5.8 (v)
obligations: Formalize F-prime-strips and the full poly-isomorphism.
Formalize the log-shell as a compact submodule of the p_v-adic field and its archimedean analogue.

IUT3.Prop1_2.content: Properties of log-links of F-prime-strips: (i) coricity of the associated D-prime-strips; (ii) simultaneous compatibility with ring structures of domain and codomain; (iii) log-volume compatibility; (iv) Kummer isomorphisms are not compatible with the log-link; (v) holomorphic log-shells are compact and contain the images of units and of the relevant invariants; (vi) to (viii) mono-analytic log-shells, with Ism-orbits at nonarchimedean v and {±1}-orbits on direct factors at archimedean v; (ix) coric holomorphic log-shells; (x) the Frobenius-picture.
obligations: Prove compactness of log-shells.
Prove log-volume compatibility of the log-link.
Model the failure of Kummer compatibility (iv) as a precise non-commutativity statement.

IUT3.Prop1_2.x.content: Frobenius-picture: a Z-indexed chain of full log-links of F-prime-strips induces chains of full poly-isomorphisms of D- and D^⊢-prime-strips, depicted as an oriented graph with a horizontal chain of vertices and Kummer arrows to a coric vertex ◦. The graph admits a Z translation symmetry fixing ◦ but no arbitrary permutation symmetries; for instance no automorphism swaps two adjacent vertices.
explicit_hypotheses: a collection of distinct F-prime-strips indexed by Z linked by full log-links
IUT3.Prop1_2.x.conclusion: Chains of full poly-isomorphisms; Z-action; no adjacent swap.
obligations: Formalize the oriented graph and verify that its automorphism group is Z (a purely combinatorial obligation once the graph is fixed).

IUT3.Rem1_2_2.content: The Frobenius-picture diagram is far from commutative; coric holomorphic log-shells satisfy only upper semi-commutativity; there is no lower semi-commutativity; the diagram is commutative with respect to log-volumes.
obligations: Make 'upper semi-commutativity' precise as a containment of images along different paths.
ambiguities: 'commutative with respect to log-volumes' is not defined as a formal property; reading it as equality of log-volumes of images along different paths is an interpretation.

IUT3.Prop1_3.content: Log-links between Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters: (i) built from a fixed full log-link of F-prime-strips; (ii) coricity of the associated D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater; (iii) analogues of Prop 1.2; (iv) Frobenius-picture with Z-action and no adjacent swap.
explicit_hypotheses: Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters relative to fixed initial Θ-data
obligations: Formalize Hodge theaters (vocabulary not yet in the project).

IUT3.Def1_4.content: The log-theta-lattice: Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters indexed by (n,m) ∈ Z×Z, vertical arrows the full log-links (n,m) → (n,m+1), horizontal arrows the Θ^{×μ}-links (non-Gaussian) or Θ^{×μ}_gau-links (Gaussian) (n,m) → (n+1,m).
explicit_hypotheses: a collection of distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters indexed by pairs of integers
obligations: Represent the lattice as a Z×Z-indexed diagram with two kinds of arrows.

IUT3.Rem1_4_1.content: (i) The squares of the log-theta-lattice are far from 1-commutative, because vertical arrows depend on local ring structures and horizontal arrows are incompatible with them. (ii) Each execution of a horizontal arrow obligates a subsequent vertical arrow, because log-shells live on the codomain of a log-link.
obligations: State non-commutativity of a square precisely (what composites are compared, at which structural level).

explicit_hypotheses: initial Θ-data (F̄/F, X_F, l, C_K, V, V^bad_mod, ε)
obligations: See the part records.

IUT3.Thm1_5.i.content: Vertical coricity: vertical arrows induce full poly-isomorphisms of the associated D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters, n fixed, m varying.
IUT3.Thm1_5.i.conclusion: Full poly-isomorphisms n,m HT^{D-Θ±ellNF} ≅ n,m+1 HT^{D-Θ±ellNF}.
obligations: Show the D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater is unchanged up to full poly-isomorphism by a log-link.

IUT3.Thm1_5.ii.content: Horizontal coricity: horizontal arrows induce full poly-isomorphisms of the F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strips n,m 𝔉_△^{⊢×μ} → n+1,m 𝔉_△^{⊢×μ}, m fixed.
obligations: Formalize F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strips and the Θ^{×μ}-link.

IUT3.Thm1_5.iii.content: Bi-coric F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strips F^{⊢×μ}_△(n,m D^⊢_△): poly-isomorphisms induced by (i) along columns and by (ii) along rows; the vertical collection is in general strictly smaller than the horizontal one, and the horizontal poly-isomorphisms are not full. Composition gives poly-isomorphisms for arbitrary (n,m), (n',m'). Kummer isomorphisms n,m 𝔉^{⊢×μ}_△ ≅ F^{⊢×μ}_△(n,m D^⊢_△) compatible with (ii).
IUT3.Thm1_5.iii.conclusion: F^{⊢×μ}_△(n,m D^⊢_△), up to a certain class of isomorphisms, is invariant under both kinds of arrows.
external_dependencies: IUTchII: Cor 4.5 (ii), (iii), Cor 4.6 (i), Cor 4.10 (i), Def 4.9, Remark 1.8.1
obligations: Identify the class of isomorphisms relative to which the bi-coric strip is 'invariant'.
Prove the stated strict containment of poly-isomorphism collections.
ambiguities: 'regarded up to a certain class of isomorphisms' (page 49 to 50) is not given an explicit description in the statement.

IUT3.Thm1_5.iv.content: Bi-coric mono-analytic log-shells: the poly-isomorphisms of (iii) induce poly-isomorphisms of mono-analytic log-shells for arbitrary (n,m), (n',m'), compatible with Prop 1.2 (viii); natural poly-isomorphisms to the holomorphic log-shell I_{n,m 𝔉_△}.
IUT3.Thm1_5.iv.conclusion: Poly-isomorphisms of log-shell pairs I ⊆ log(−).
obligations: Formalize log-shells and the induced poly-isomorphisms.

IUT3.Thm1_5.v.content: Bi-coric mono-analytic global realified Frobenioids D^⊩(n,m D^⊢_△), with isomorphisms of collections of data compatible with R_{>0}-orbits of local isomorphisms.
IUT3.Thm1_5.v.conclusion: Isomorphisms of global realified Frobenioid data across the lattice.
obligations: Formalize global realified Frobenioids.

IUT3.Rem1_5_4.content: Splits describing one arithmetic holomorphic structure (vertical line) from another into (a) passing from Frobenius-like to étale-like structures via Kummer isomorphisms and (b) transporting étale-like structures by multiradiality. Indeterminacies from (a) are called Kummer-detachment indeterminacies, those from (b) étale-transport indeterminacies. Examples: automorphisms of G_v not of scheme-theoretic origin (étale-transport); the non-commutative Frobenius-picture and the Ẑ^× indeterminacies of Remark 1.4.2 (Kummer-detachment).
obligations: Give a precise definition of each indeterminacy class as a set of maps or a group action.
ambiguities: Pages 52 to 55 (Remarks 1.5.1 to 1.5.3) were not read; Remark 1.5.4 cites Remark 1.5.2 (ii), which is therefore cited but not read.

IUT3.Def2_4.content: Defines F^{⊩⊥}- and F^{⊩▶}-prime-strips from F^⊩-prime-strips by passing to the split-monoid sub- and quotient portions O^⊥ ⊆ O^▷, and morphisms as isomorphisms of the data.
obligations: Formalize F^⊩-prime-strips.

IUT3.Rem2_4_2.content: (i) Pilot objects for F^{⊩▶}-prime-strips. (ii) Weights r_v = [(F_mod)_v : Q_{v_Q}]·log(p_v) at good v and [(F_mod)_v : Q_{v_Q}]·ord_v(q_v)·log(p_v) at bad v; r^▶_v = −r_v / Σ_{w ∈ V^bad} r_w. (iii) to (v) an ordered monoid M ≅ R determines collections (M, {M_v}, {ρ_{M_v}}). (vi) comparing positive and negative pilot elements requires an ambient category in which the steps are invertible, which renders degree comparisons meaningless.
obligations: Fix the normalization of ord_v and of r_v used later in Cor 3.12.

IUT3.Prop3_1.content: Local holomorphic tensor packets: for a capsule A of F-prime-strips, log(^A F_{v_Q}) = ⊗_{α ∈ A} log(^α F_{v_Q}), with direct sum decompositions into fields and integral structures given by tensor products of rings of integers; Q-spans I^Q.
IUT3.Prop3_1.conclusion: Construction of tensor packets with ring and integral structures.
obligations: Formalize topological tensor products of local fields and their decomposition into products of fields.

IUT3.Rem3_1_1.content: (ii) Normalized weights for the components of the packets. (iii) measure-space formalism and direct product regions S = ∏_v S_v with S_v compact of positive measure. (iv) For direct product regions, (1/N_E)·μ^log_E(S) = Σ_v (1/N_v)·μ^log_v(S_v), N_E = ∏ N_v.
IUT3.Rem3_1_1.conclusion: Normalizations and a computation for direct product regions.
obligations: Verify the (iv) identity as a product-measure computation (elementary once the spaces are fixed).
ambiguities: The value set of μ_E is R_{≥0} ∪ {+∞}; finiteness for the regions used later is not stated at this point.

IUT3.Prop3_2.content: Local mono-analytic tensor packets for n-capsules of D^⊢-prime-strips: (i) poly-isomorphisms to the holomorphic packets of Prop 3.1; (ii) mono-analytic integral structures I(^α D^⊢_{v_Q}) and Q-spans I^Q.
obligations: Formalize the poly-isomorphisms and the integral structures.

IUT3.Prop3_3.content: Global tensor packets: the copies of (M_mod)_α embed diagonally into the product of local holomorphic packets over v_Q.
obligations: Formalize number field embeddings into products of local packets.

IUT3.Prop3_4.content: (i) single-packet monoids; (ii) LGP-monoids Ψ_{F_LGP}: for j ∈ {1, ..., l*}, the j-th component acts on I^Q(S^±_{j+1},j; F_v) via the theta values q^{j²}.
obligations: Formalize processions and the index sets S^±_{j+1}.

IUT3.Prop3_5.content: (i) Vertically coric LGP-monoids and their Kummer isomorphisms. (ii) Upper semi-compatibility of the log-Kummer correspondence: (a) at nonarchimedean v_Q the mono-analytic integral structure contains the Kummer images of units, also after the m'-th iterate of the log-link; (b) at archimedean v_Q the closed unit ball contains the units and the closed balls of radius π, with a surjection via iterates; (c) at bad v the splitting monoids are mutually compatible up to roots of unity, which via the log-link is 'addition by zero'. Invariance under the column translation symmetry.
obligations: State and prove the containments (a), (b) as inclusions of explicit subsets of p-adic and complex fields.
Prove that roots of unity in the domain map to 0 under the p-adic logarithm (c).

IUT3.Prop3_7.content: F^⊩-prime-strips (F^⊩_MOD)_α, (F^⊩_mod)_α; global realified Frobenioids C^⊩_LGP and C^⊩_lgp; F^{⊩▶}_LGP and F^{⊩▶}_lgp prime-strips; an algorithm constructing objects of C^⊩_lgp and C^⊩_LGP from local fractional ideals generated by the monoids Ψ_{F_lgp} at bad v. Proof: follows immediately from the definitions and cited references.
obligations: Formalize the global realified Frobenioids and the realification functor.

IUT3.Def3_8.content: Θ-pilot and q-pilot objects; Θ^{×μ}_LGP- and Θ^{×μ}_lgp-links; LGP- and lgp-Gaussian log-theta-lattices.
obligations: See part records.

IUT3.Def3_8.i.content: Θ-pilot object: the object of ∏_{j ∈ F*_l} (†F_MOD)_j or ∏_j (†F_mod)_j, or its realification in †C^⊩_LGP or †C^⊩_lgp, determined by any collection over v ∈ V^bad of generators up to torsion of Ψ^⊥_{F_lgp}(†HT)_v. q-pilot object: the object of †C^⊩_△ determined by generators up to torsion of the splitting monoid of †F^⊢_{△,v}, concretely by the q_v for v ∈ V^bad.
obligations: Show the object is independent of the choice of generators up to torsion (implicit in 'determined by any collection').
ambiguities: 'determined by any collection' asserts independence of the choice; no argument is given at this point.

IUT3.Def3_8.ii.content: Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link †HT → *HT relative to a log-link ‡HT → †HT: the full poly-isomorphism of F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strips †𝔉_LGP^{⊩▶×μ} ≅ *𝔉_△^{⊩▶×μ}; similarly the Θ^{×μ}_lgp-link.
obligations: Formalize F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strips and full poly-isomorphisms between them.

IUT3.Def3_8.iii.content: LGP-Gaussian (respectively lgp-Gaussian) log-theta-lattice: vertical arrows full log-links; the horizontal arrow from (n,m) to (n+1,m) is the Θ^{×μ}_LGP- (respectively Θ^{×μ}_lgp-) link relative to the full log-link (n,m−1) → (n,m).
obligations: Represent the lattice with this dependence of horizontal arrows on the vertical arrow below.

IUT3.Rem3_8_1.content: Both the Θ^{×μ}_LGP- and Θ^{×μ}_lgp-links map Θ-pilot objects to q-pilot objects; the theory mainly uses the LGP-Gaussian lattice.
obligations: Check from the definitions that the full poly-isomorphism carries the Θ-pilot object to the q-pilot object.

IUT3.Prop3_9.content: Log-volumes for packets and processions. Proof: 'follow immediately from the definitions'.
obligations: See part records.

IUT3.Prop3_9.i.content: Packet-normalized log-volumes μ^log_{α,v_Q}, μ^log_{A,v_Q}, μ^log_{A,α,v} : M(I^Q(−)) → R, where M(−) is the set of nonempty compact open subsets (nonarchimedean) or compact closures of nonempty open subsets (archimedean). The local holomorphic integral structures have log-volume 0; multiplying by p_v adds −log(p_v) (nonarchimedean); multiplying by e adds 1 (archimedean). μ^log_{A,v_Q} is invariant under permutations of A. Procession-normalization: average over the capsules of a procession.
IUT3.Prop3_9.i.conclusion: Existence of normalized log-volume maps with the stated normalizations.
obligations: Construct μ^log as the logarithm of a Haar measure normalized so that the integral structure has measure 1.
Check the scaling rule: multiplication by p_v multiplies Haar measure by the normalized absolute value, so log-volume shifts by −log(p_v) only under a specific weighting; record the weighting used.
Define the procession-normalized log-volume as an explicit average.
ambiguities: The multiplication-by-p_v rule depends on the normalized weights of Remark 3.1.1 (ii); the exact weighting under which it holds for a tensor packet with several components is stated by reference, not derived on the page.

IUT3.Prop3_9.ii.content: Mono-analytic compatibility: applying p_v-adic or radial log-volumes on mono-analytic log-shells, adjusted for the discrepancy between holomorphic and mono-analytic integral structures (Remark 3.9.1), gives log-volumes on M(I^Q(^α D^⊢_{v_Q})) etc. compatible with (i) via the natural poly-isomorphisms of Prop 3.2 (i), constructible by a functorial algorithm from D^⊢-prime-strips; procession-normalized versions compatible likewise; similarly for F^{⊢×μ}.
IUT3.Prop3_9.ii.conclusion: Compatibility of mono-analytic and holomorphic log-volumes under the poly-isomorphisms.
obligations: Prove invariance of the log-volume under every isomorphism in the poly-isomorphism (Ism at nonarchimedean v, independent ±1 at archimedean v).
Make the 'adjusting appropriately' of the discrepancy explicit (Remark 3.9.1 gives a factor of 2 at archimedean places).

IUT3.Prop3_9.iii.content: Global log-volume μ^log_{A,V_Q} on elements of ∏ M(I^Q(^A F_{v_Q})) with zero log-volume at all but finitely many v_Q, obtained by summing; invariant under multiplication by (M_mod)_α = (M_MOD)_α and permutations of A; for objects J = {J_v} of (F_mod)_α its value equals the degree of the associated arithmetic line bundle, relative to a suitable normalization.
IUT3.Prop3_9.iii.conclusion: Global log-volume equals arithmetic degree up to normalization.
obligations: Prove invariance under multiplication by number field elements (product formula).
Fix the normalization and prove equality with the degree.
ambiguities: 'relative to a suitable normalization' (page 117) is not specified; the sign and scaling of the comparison with the degree are left implicit.

IUT3.Prop3_9.iv.content: log-link compatibility: (a) the log-volumes of (i) to (iii) determine log-volumes on the I^Q((−)) that appear in the construction of the local and global LGP and lgp monoids and Frobenioids at (n,m), relative to the log-link (n,m−1) → (n,m); (b) at the level of Q-spans of log-shells the log-volumes indexed by (n,m) are compatible with those indexed by (n,m−1) in the sense of Props 1.2 (iii), 1.3 (iii).
IUT3.Prop3_9.iv.conclusion: Log-volumes are compatible along each column.
obligations: Prove the log-volume compatibility of the p-adic logarithm on the relevant compact sets (Remark 3.9.4 (iii) gives the local mechanism).

IUT3.Rem3_9_1.content: Concrete description: I_i = (p*)^{-1}·log(O^×_{k_i}); at archimedean places C ⊗_R C ≅ C ⊕ C is compatible with metrics up to a factor of 2.
obligations: Fix the archimedean factor of 2 in the normalization of Prop 3.9 (ii).

IUT3.Rem3_9_3.content: Weights in the procession-normalization must be equal: for j' ≤ j1, j2 the same log-shell labeled j' occurs in capsules S^±_{j1+1} and S^±_{j2+1}, and compatibility with the inclusion morphisms of the procession forces equal weights.
IUT3.Rem3_9_3.conclusion: Only plain averages are compatible with the procession inclusions.
obligations: State precisely what compatibility with inclusion morphisms means for a weighted average, then prove that it forces equal weights.
ambiguities: The argument does not specify which quantity must be preserved under inclusions; the conclusion 'no choice but to assign the same weights' depends on that specification.

IUT3.Rem3_9_4.content: (i) Sub(M), Fn(M), the integral ∫ : Fn(M) → R_{≥0} and the quotient Rss(M) ≅ R_{≥0}, R_{>0}-equivariant. (ii) If log rescaled volumes by λ ≠ 1, log-volumes would only be defined in R / Z·log λ. (iii) μ_k(S) = μ_k(log_k(S)) for suitable compact S ⊆ O_k^×. (iv) at bad v, the submonoid O_k^× × q^N; the chain k ⇝ O_k^× × q^N ⇝ O_k^× ⇝ log_k(O_k^×) ⇝ k induces R_{>0}-equivariant isomorphisms of Rss and an embedding N → R ∪ {−∞} sending 1 to −log(q), with log(q) = ord_v(q_v)·log(p_v). (v), (vi) tensor products and archimedean case.
IUT3.Rem3_9_4.conclusion: Explicit formulation of log-link compatibility of log-volumes.
obligations: Prove μ(S) = μ(log S) for the relevant compact S (a change-of-variables statement for the p-adic logarithm on a domain where it is injective and measure preserving).
ambiguities: Value set R ∪ {−∞} appears here (page 124) for log-volumes of Rss, while Cor 3.12 uses R ∪ {+∞}.

IUT3.Rem3_9_5.content: Holomorphic hulls and related discussion (i) to (x).
obligations: See part records.

IUT3.Rem3_9_5.i.content: For a subset U of I^Q(−) that contains a relatively compact subset of finite log-volume: if U is relatively compact, its holomorphic hull is the smallest subset λ·O (λ with every component nonzero in the direct sum decomposition) containing U; otherwise the hull is all of I^Q(−). 'One verifies immediately that the holomorphic hull is well-defined.'
obligations: Prove existence and uniqueness of a smallest λ·O containing a relatively compact U (componentwise this is the smallest scaled ring of integers containing the projection, which exists by discreteness of the value group).
Prove the hull is independent of the choice of λ among those giving the same set.
ambiguities: At archimedean components the ring O is a closed unit ball in C; 'smallest λ·O' then refers to the smallest closed ball, which exists by compactness; the text does not separate the cases.

IUT3.Rem3_9_5.ii.content: P = direct product regions, H = hulls (proper subsets), H ⊆ P. Forming the hull gives φ : P → H characterized uniquely by (P1) φ(H) = H, (P2) P ⊆ φ(P), (P3) monotone; since intersections of elements of H of finite log-volume lie in H, φ(P) = ⋂_{H ∈ H, H ⊇ P} H.
IUT3.Rem3_9_5.ii.conclusion: Uniqueness of φ and the intersection formula.
obligations: Done in Lean for arbitrary families of sets, in module IUT.PaperIII.Remark3_9_5.HullOperator: (P1) to (P3) alone imply the intersection formula and uniqueness (IsHullMap.eq_sInter, IsHullMap.unique); the intersection-closure hypothesis gives existence (isHullMap_sInter). This is not a formalization of hulls of tensor packets.
Remaining: prove the intersection-closure property for actual hulls of finite log-volume.
ambiguities: Assessment: the order-theoretic check shows the formula follows from (P1) to (P3) without the intersection hypothesis; the hypothesis is needed only for existence. The text presents it as the reason for the formula.

IUT3.Rem3_9_5.iii_iv.content: Hull-approximants Φ(P), Ξ(P); in general P ⊆ φ(P) is strict in log-volume. Example: I = Q_p × Q_p, H0 = Z_p × Z_p, H1 = p^{-1}Z_p × pZ_p, P = H0 ∪ ({p^{-1}} × Z_p), H_P = p^{-1}Z_p × Z_p; μ_I(P) = μ_I(H0) = 1 < 2 − p^{-1} = μ_I(H0 ∪ H1).
IUT3.Rem3_9_5.iii_iv.conclusion: Strictness of the inequality μ^log(P) < μ^log(φ(P)) in examples.
obligations: Verify the example: μ(H1) = p·p^{-1} = 1, μ(H0 ∩ H1) = μ(Z_p × pZ_p) = p^{-1}, so μ(H0 ∪ H1) = 2 − p^{-1}; μ({p^{-1}} × Z_p) = 0.

IUT3.Rem3_9_5.vii.content: Obstructions (Ob1) to (Ob9): O^×-multiple indeterminacy; hulls as localizations of arithmetic vector bundles; passage to det and M-th tensor powers to compare with the q-pilot line bundle (Ob4); independence of possibilities via bounded families φ(P_B) (Ob5); hull-approximants (Ob6); why log-volumes alone do not suffice (Ob7); vertical shifts (Ob8); Rss bijection (Ob9).
IUT3.Rem3_9_5.vii.conclusion: Interpretive discussion of why hulls, determinants and log-volumes are used.
obligations: Make precise the comparison of the determinant of a rank r hull with the q-pilot line bundle, including how the tensor power M rescales log-volume.
ambiguities: (Ob4): the effect of the M-th tensor power on the normalized log-volume is not written as a formula.

IUT3.Rem3_9_5.viii_x.content: Subquotient operations (sQ1) to (sQ5); the 'closed loop' of (cQ3), (cQ4) versus (iQ5); why a category of regions cannot replace arithmetic line bundles.
obligations: Define the subquotient operations as maps between explicit sets so that the 'closed loop' becomes a checkable composite.

IUT3.Rem3_9_7.content: Log-volumes defined as infima may take the value −∞; inverse-system formulations.
obligations: Fix the extended value set used for log-volumes of hulls.
ambiguities: Cor 3.12 uses R ∪ {+∞} for −|log(Θ)|; this remark allows −∞ for inf-defined volumes. The two conventions concern different quantities but are not reconciled explicitly.

IUT3.Prop3_10.content: (i) Vertically coric global Frobenioids and their Kummer isomorphisms. (ii) Non-interference: (M_MOD)_α ∩ ∏_v Ψ_log equals the roots of unity, via the fact that elements of a number field that are units at all places are roots of unity. (iii) The F_MOD isomorphisms and F^{⊩⊥}_LGP-prime-strips are mutually compatible with the log-links.
external_dependencies: Lang: Algebraic number theory (1970), page 144, proof of Theorem 5
obligations: Prove (ii) from the cited result of Lang; whether Mathlib contains it was not checked.

IUT3.Rem3_10_1.content: F_mod is only upper semi-compatible with log-links, in contrast to F_MOD; Fig. 3.2 compares them.
obligations: State the upper semi-compatibility of F_mod as a containment.

IUT3.Thm3_11.content: Multiradial algorithms via LGP-monoids and Frobenioids, for an LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice. Three parts: (i) multiradial representation, (ii) log-Kummer correspondence, (iii) Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link compatibility. Proof: the assertions 'follow immediately from the definitions and the references quoted'. Not stated as a Lean Prop: the vocabulary does not exist.

a collection of distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters {n,m HT}_{n,m ∈ Z} arising from an LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice
implicit_hypotheses: the D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater n,◦HT is determined up to isomorphism by vertical coricity (Thm 1.5 (i), Rem 3.8.2)

IUTchII: Cor 4.6 (iii), (iv), Cor 4.7 (iii), Cor 4.8 (i) to (iii), Cor 4.10 (i), (iv), Cor 4.11 (i) to (iii), Props 4.2 (i), 4.4 (i)
obligations: See part records; docs/THEOREM_3_11.md separates each claim.

IUT3.Thm3_11.i.content: Multiradial representation: from the procession Prc(n,◦D^⊢_T) obtained via IUTchI Prop 6.9 (ii), data (a), (b), (c) are constructed; n,◦R^LGP denotes these data regarded up to (Ind1), (Ind2); n,◦R^LGP is constructible by an algorithm in the procession, functorial in isomorphisms of processions; permutation symmetries of the étale-picture induce compatible poly-isomorphisms Prc(n) ≅ Prc(n') and n,◦R ≅ n',◦R, compatible with the bi-coricity poly-isomorphisms n,◦D^⊢_0 ≅ n',◦D^⊢_0.
IUT3.Thm3_11.i.conclusion: Existence of an algorithm producing n,◦R^LGP, functoriality, and compatibility with the étale-picture symmetries.
external_dependencies: IUTchI: Def 3.1, Prop 6.9 (ii), Cor 6.10 (iii), Def 5.2 (vi), (viii), Example 5.1 (v)
IUTchII: Cor 4.6 (iii), (iv), Cor 4.7 (iii), Cor 4.8 (i) to (iii), Cor 4.10 (i), (iv), Cor 4.11 (i) to (iii), Props 4.2 (i), 4.4 (i)
obligations: Define 'algorithm in the procession' as a functor from a groupoid of processions.
Prove functoriality.
Prove compatibility of the permutation-symmetry poly-isomorphisms with the bi-coricity ones.
ambiguities: 'algorithm' and 'functorial' are used in the sense of IUTchI; their exact categorical meaning is not restated.

IUT3.Thm3_11.i.a.content: For v ∈ V over v_Q ∈ V_Q and j ∈ |F_l|: mono-analytic integral structures I(S^±_{j+1}; n,◦D^⊢_{v_Q}) ⊆ I^Q(S^±_{j+1}; n,◦D^⊢_{v_Q}) and I(S^±_{j+1},j; n,◦D^⊢_v) ⊆ I^Q(...), equipped with the procession-normalized mono-analytic log-volumes of Prop 3.9 (ii).
IUT3.Thm3_11.i.a.conclusion: Construction of local data with log-volumes.
obligations: Construct these modules from D^⊢-prime-strips alone (mono-analyticity).
ambiguities: Indexed by j ∈ |F_l| (page 153), while Cor 3.12 averages over j ∈ F*_l (pages 173, 181).

IUT3.Thm3_11.i.b.content: For v ∈ V^bad: the splitting monoid Ψ^⊥_LGP(n,◦HT)_v of Prop 3.5 (ii)(c), regarded via natural poly-isomorphisms I^Q(S^±_{j+1},j; n,◦D^⊢_v) ≅ I^Q(S^±_{j+1},j F^{⊢×μ}(n,◦D_≻)_v) ≅ I^Q(S^±_{j+1},j F(n,◦D_≻)_v), j ∈ F*_l, as a subset of ∏_{j ∈ F*_l} I^Q(...) with a multiplicative action on that product.
IUT3.Thm3_11.i.b.conclusion: Construction of the splitting monoid acting on the product of packets.
obligations: Construct the action and show it is well defined relative to the poly-isomorphisms (each isomorphism in the poly-isomorphism must give the same subset, or the subset must be read up to the poly-isomorphism).

IUT3.Thm3_11.i.c.content: For j ∈ F*_l: the number field M_MOD(n,◦HT)_j = M_mod(n,◦HT)_j ⊆ I^Q(S^±_{j+1}; n,◦D^⊢_{V_Q}) := ∏_{v_Q} I^Q(...), with natural isomorphisms F_MOD ≅ F_mod and F^R_MOD ≅ F^R_mod of global non-realified and realified Frobenioids, whose global degrees may be computed by the log-volumes of (a) (Prop 3.9 (iii)).
IUT3.Thm3_11.i.c.conclusion: Global data with degrees computed by log-volumes.
obligations: Prove degree equals global log-volume, with the normalization of Prop 3.9 (iii) made explicit.
ambiguities: Inherits 'relative to a suitable normalization' from Prop 3.9 (iii).

IUT3.Thm3_11.i.Ind1.content: (Ind1): indeterminacies induced by the automorphisms of the procession of D^⊢-prime-strips Prc(n,◦D^⊢_T).
obligations: Identify Aut(Prc) explicitly and its action on the data (a), (b), (c).
ambiguities: Whether Ind1 includes only permutations of labels compatible with the procession inclusions or also automorphisms of each D^⊢-prime-strip is not stated on the page.

IUT3.Thm3_11.i.Ind2.content: (Ind2): for each v_Q ∈ V^non_Q (respectively V^arc_Q), the action of independent copies of Ism (respectively of the order 2 automorphisms whose orbit is the poly-automorphism of Prop 1.2 (vii)) on each direct summand of the j+1 tensor factors defining I^Q(S^±_{j+1}; n,◦D^⊢_{v_Q}); the number of direct summands equals the number of v ∈ V over v_Q.
obligations: Define the group ∏ Ism acting on the tensor packet and prove it preserves the procession-normalized log-volume.

IUT3.Thm3_11.ii.content: log-Kummer correspondence: for n, m ∈ Z, the Kummer isomorphisms of labeled data (Ψ_cns, π_1^{κ-sol} ⟲ M_{∞κ}, M̄_mod) induce isomorphisms between the vertically coric data (a), (b), (c) of (i), not yet subjected to Ind1, Ind2, and the corresponding data from each n,m HT.
IUT3.Thm3_11.ii.conclusion: Isomorphisms (a), (b), (c), their mutual compatibility as m varies, Ind3, and log-volume compatibility.
external_dependencies: IUTchI: Def 3.1, Prop 6.9 (ii), Cor 6.10 (iii), Def 5.2 (vi), (viii), Example 5.1 (v)
IUTchII: Cor 4.6 (iii), (iv), Cor 4.7 (iii), Cor 4.8 (i) to (iii), Cor 4.10 (i), (iv), Cor 4.11 (i) to (iii), Props 4.2 (i), 4.4 (i)
obligations: See sub-part records.

IUT3.Thm3_11.ii.a.content: For v over v_Q, j ∈ |F_l|: isomorphisms I(S^±_{j+1}; n,m F_{v_Q}) ≅ I(...; n,m F^{⊢×μ}_{v_Q}) ≅ I(...; n,◦D^⊢_{v_Q}), similarly for Q-spans and for the j-indexed versions, all compatible with the respective log-volumes (Prop 3.9 (ii)).
IUT3.Thm3_11.ii.a.conclusion: Isomorphisms of local packets compatible with log-volumes.
obligations: Prove each isomorphism preserves log-volume.

IUT3.Thm3_11.ii.b.content: For v ∈ V^bad: isomorphisms of splitting monoids Ψ^⊥_{F_LGP}(n,m HT)_v ≅ Ψ^⊥_LGP(n,◦HT)_v.
obligations: Construct the isomorphism from the Kummer isomorphisms.

IUT3.Thm3_11.ii.c.content: For j ∈ F*_l: isomorphisms of number fields and of global non-realified and realified Frobenioids (MOD and mod versions), compatible with the natural MOD/mod isomorphisms; the third line induces isomorphisms of C^⊩_LGP and C^⊩_lgp.
obligations: Construct the isomorphisms and check compatibility with MOD/mod identifications.

IUT3.Thm3_11.ii.mutual.content: As m varies, the isomorphisms of (b) and of the first line of (c) are mutually compatible relative to the log-links of the n-th column: the only portions possibly related via log-links are roots of unity, which map to addition by zero. This implies mutual compatibility for the second and third lines of (c) involving MOD, but not those involving mod.
IUT3.Thm3_11.ii.mutual.conclusion: Mutual compatibility along the column for (b) and MOD parts of (c).
obligations: Prove: if x lies in both the domain of the log-link and the image of (b) or (c line 1), then x is a root of unity and log(x) = 0.

IUT3.Thm3_11.ii.Ind3.content: (Ind3): as m varies, the isomorphisms of (a) are only 'upper semi-compatible' relative to the log-links of the n-th column, via natural inclusions at nonarchimedean v_Q and natural surjections at archimedean v_Q (Prop 3.5 (ii) (a), (b)). Finally, the isomorphisms of (a) are precisely compatible with log-volumes along the column (Prop 3.9 (iv)).
IUT3.Thm3_11.ii.Ind3.conclusion: Ind3 as an indeterminacy of containment type; exact compatibility of log-volumes.
obligations: Express Ind3 as: the image of any admissible region under any composite path lies in a fixed region (inclusion) so that log-volume is bounded above.
Reconcile 'upper semi-compatible' isomorphisms with 'precisely compatible' log-volumes: the latter must refer to log-volumes of corresponding sets, the former to containment of different sets.
ambiguities: Ind3 is described as an indeterminacy but defined as a semi-compatibility property; the set of maps it ranges over is not specified.

IUT3.Thm3_11.iii.content: Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link compatibility of the Kummer isomorphisms of (ii) with the horizontal arrows.
external_dependencies: IUTchI: Def 3.1, Prop 6.9 (ii), Cor 6.10 (iii), Def 5.2 (vi), (viii), Example 5.1 (v)
IUTchII: Cor 4.6 (iii), (iv), Cor 4.7 (iii), Cor 4.8 (i) to (iii), Cor 4.10 (i), (iv), Cor 4.11 (i) to (iii), Props 4.2 (i), 4.4 (i)
obligations: See sub-part records.

IUT3.Thm3_11.iii.a.content: Applying the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry gives a Kummer isomorphism n,m 𝔉^{⊢×μ}_△ ≅ F^{⊢×μ}_△(n,◦D^⊢_△); relative to it, the full poly-isomorphism F^{⊢×μ}_△(n,◦D^⊢_△) ≅ F^{⊢×μ}_△(n+1,◦D^⊢_△) is compatible with the full poly-isomorphism n,m 𝔉^{⊢×μ}_△ ≅ n+1,m 𝔉^{⊢×μ}_△ induced by the horizontal arrows.
obligations: Show that conjugating the horizontal full poly-isomorphism by the Kummer isomorphisms gives exactly the full poly-isomorphism of the coric strips (equality of sets of isomorphisms).

IUT3.Thm3_11.iii.b.content: The F^⊩-prime-strips n,m 𝔉_env^⊩, 𝔉_env^⊩(n,◦D_>) admit natural isomorphisms of associated F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strips; relative to these and (a), the full poly-isomorphism of env strips is compatible with the horizontal full poly-isomorphism.
obligations: As in (a), for env strips.

IUT3.Thm3_11.iii.c.content: The data n,◦R of Cor 2.3 (ii) relate via Kummer isomorphisms and poly-isomorphisms of projective systems of mono-theta environments to data from n,m HT at V^bad. The algorithmic construction of these and of n,◦R ≅ n+1,◦R induced by any étale-picture permutation symmetry is compatible with the horizontal arrows, i.e., stabilized/equivariant/functorial with respect to arbitrary automorphisms of domain and codomain; the evaluation maps in (ii)(b) are compatible up to Ind1, Ind2, Ind3.
IUT3.Thm3_11.iii.c.conclusion: Compatibility of theta-function data and evaluation maps with horizontal arrows up to Ind1 to Ind3.
obligations: Define 'stabilized/equivariant/functorial with respect to arbitrary automorphisms' as a precise equivariance property.
Prove the evaluation maps commute with the horizontal arrows modulo the action of Ind1 × Ind2 and up to the containments of Ind3.
ambiguities: 'compatible up to the indeterminacies (Ind1), (Ind2), (Ind3)' does not say whether the indeterminacies act jointly or separately, nor whether compatibility means equality of orbits or containment.

IUT3.Thm3_11.iii.d.content: Same as (c) for the Kummer isomorphisms of the κ-coric (number field) data, the gluing of IUTchII Cor 4.6 (iv), and the poly-isomorphisms between data [π_1^{κ-sol} ⟲ M_{∞κ} → M_{∞κv} ⊆ M_{∞κ×v}] induced by permutation symmetries.
IUT3.Thm3_11.iii.d.conclusion: Compatibility of number field data with horizontal arrows up to Ind1 to Ind3.
obligations: As in (c).
ambiguities: As in (c).

IUT3.Rem3_11_1.content: Interpretation of Thm 3.11: (ii) the q-pilot could be replaced by q^λ; the codomain is coric. (iii) definitions of IPL (input prime-strip link) and SHE (simultaneous holomorphic expressibility); SHE corresponds to a closed loop of the subquotient operations of Rem 3.9.5. (iv) APT and HIS. (v) input/output summary. (vi), (vii) naive alternatives: distinct labels give IPL but not SHE; forced identification gives SHE but not IPL. (viii) why these alternatives do not serve Cor 3.12.
IUT3.Rem3_11_1.conclusion: Definitions of the properties IPL, SHE, APT, HIS used in Cor 3.12 Step (xi).
obligations: Give IPL and SHE as precise properties of an algorithm (input type, output type, the relation to be preserved).
ambiguities: IPL and SHE are stated informally; their formal content (which map, which structure) is the main missing vocabulary for Cor 3.12.

IUT3.Rem3_11_3.content: (i) Squares of the lattice are far from 1-commutative but commute for bi-coric data; (ii) to (iv) a single Θ-link is used; vertical shift of the domain of the horizontal arrow.
obligations: Specify the forgetful functor after which squares commute.

IUT3.Rem3_11_4.content: Invisible indeterminacies: μ_{2l} acting on theta values {q^{j²}}_{j=1..l*} (Fig. 3.4) and μ(F_mod^×) acting on copies of F_mod^× (Fig. 3.5); Kummer isomorphisms are determined by cyclotome isomorphisms and Galois actions (FrdII Def 2.1 (ii)); these invisible indeterminacies are an analogue of Ind3 for the data of (ii)(b), (c); multiradiality asserts that Ind1, Ind2 have no effect on the geometric containers underlying (ii)(b), (c).
obligations: State the invisible indeterminacies as group actions and show they act trivially after evaluation.

IUT3.Cor3_12.content: Log-volume estimates for Θ-pilot objects. In the situation of Thm 3.11, −|log(Θ)| ≥ −|log(q)|, with −|log(Θ)| ∈ R. Proof: an opening reduction and Steps (i) to (xii). Not stated as a Lean Prop. The file IUT/PaperIII/Corollary312/Numerical.lean treats only the numerical layer and is not a formalization of this corollary.
IUT3.Cor3_12.conclusion: −|log(Θ)| ∈ R and −|log(Θ)| ≥ −|log(q)|; equivalently C_Θ ≥ −1 for every real C_Θ with −|log(Θ)| ≤ C_Θ·|log(q)|.
obligations: See step records; docs/COR312_ANALYSIS.md.

IUT3.Cor3_12.Statement.content: −|log(Θ)| ∈ R ∪ {+∞} is the procession-normalized mono-analytic log-volume (average over j ∈ F*_l) of the holomorphic hull of the union of the possible images of a Θ-pilot object, relative to the Kummer isomorphisms of Thm 3.11 (ii), in the multiradial representation of Thm 3.11 (i), subject to Ind1, Ind2, Ind3. −|log(q)| ∈ R is the procession-normalized mono-analytic log-volume of the image of a q-pilot object, relative to the Kummer isomorphisms, in the multiradial representation, not subject to the indeterminacies; △ is the result of identifying the labels 0 and ⟨F*_l⟩. |log(q)| > 0 is 'easily computed' from the q-parameters at v ∈ V^bad (≠ ∅).
implicit_hypotheses: the union of possible images is a subset of the packets on which the hull is defined (Rem 3.9.5 (i) requires a relatively compact subset of finite log-volume)
definitions_required: possible image of a Θ-pilot object
obligations: Define the set of possible images: the orbit of the image under the group generated by Ind1 and Ind2, together with the containments allowed by Ind3.
Define the hull of the union and its log-volume.
Prove |log(q)| > 0 from ord_v(q_v) > 0 at bad v and V^bad ≠ ∅.
ambiguities: Averaging index: the statement (page 173) and Step (x) (page 181) average over j ∈ F*_l; the sets U are indexed by j ∈ |F_l| (page 174); Step (xi-d) normalizes 'with respect to j ∈ |F_l|' (page 183); Thm 3.11 (i)(a) indexes packets by j ∈ |F_l| (page 153).
The extracted text of page 174 reads 'V^bad (= ∅)'; the rendered page reads '(≠ ∅)'. This is an extraction artifact, not a discrepancy in the paper.

'possible images' and 'subject to the indeterminacies' are not defined as a set by an explicit formula; whether Ind3 enlarges each image to a containing region or acts as a separate indeterminacy is not stated.

IUT3.Cor3_12.Reduction.content: Since |log(q)| > 0 one may assume −|log(Θ)| < 0 whenever it is real. U = {n,◦U_{j,v_Q}} for j ∈ |F_l|, v_Q ∈ V_Q: unions of possible images in n,◦U^Q_{j,v_Q} = I^Q(S^±_{j+1}; n,◦D^⊢_{v_Q}). Ū = their holomorphic hulls relative to the holomorphic structure labeled n,◦. From the '[easily verified] compactness' of the 1,◦U_{j,v_Q} and the definition of log-volume, −|log(Θ)| is finite, hence negative. One may restrict to possible images that can be interpreted as an F^{⊩▶}-prime-strip.
IUT3.Cor3_12.Reduction.conclusion: Finiteness of −|log(Θ)|; WLOG negativity; restriction of possible images.
obligations: The numerical reduction is checked in Lean: IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.inequality_of_nonneg.
Prove compactness of each 1,◦U_{j,v_Q} (union over the Ind1 × Ind2 orbit, enlarged by Ind3): requires Ind1, Ind2 finite or compact and Ind3 bounded.
Prove that compactness implies the hull is a proper λ·O, hence finite log-volume.
Justify that restricting to possible images interpretable as F^{⊩▶}-prime-strips does not change the hull or only shrinks it in a way consistent with the inequality.
ambiguities: The WLOG reduction is numerical and verified in Lean (inequality_of_nonneg). The finiteness claim rests on 'easily verified compactness' (page 175), for which no argument is given.
The restriction to images interpretable as an F^{⊩▶}-prime-strip shrinks the union; the effect on the hull and hence on −|log(Θ)| is not discussed.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepI.content: Concentrate on a single Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link (0,0) → (1,0): the full poly-isomorphism 0,0 𝔉_LGP^{⊩▶×μ} ≅ 1,0 𝔉_△^{⊩▶×μ}, split into a unit portion (F^{⊢×μ}) and a value group portion (F^{⊩▶}); the value group portion maps Θ-pilot objects at (0,0) to q-pilot objects at (1,0) (Rem 3.8.1).
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepI.conclusion: Nature of the justification in the text: argument by definition.
obligations: Show the full poly-isomorphism of F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strips decomposes as a product of the unit and value group poly-isomorphisms.
Show the value group portion carries the Θ-pilot object to the q-pilot object.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepII.content: Units in 0,0 𝔉^{⊢×μ}_LGP are subject to Aut_{F^{⊢×μ}} indeterminacies (Ind1, Ind2); the cyclotomes in the Kummer theory of the étale theta function and κ-coric functions are insulated from these indeterminacies, by cyclotomic rigidity of mono-theta environments [EtTh] and by IUTchI Example 5.1 (v), Def 5.2 (vi), (viii).
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepII.conclusion: Nature of the justification in the text: citation.
obligations: Prove that the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism is invariant under Aut_{F^{⊢×μ}} (external: EtTh).

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepIII.content: Unit and value group portions on the 0-column must be related simultaneously to those on the 1-column; relating them via two different links (0,m) → (1,m) and (0,m') → (1,m'), m' ≠ m, is made practically impossible by the non-commutativity of the lattice (Rem 3.11.3 (i), (ii)). Hence a single Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link.
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepIII.conclusion: Nature of the justification in the text: assertion with interpretive argument.
obligations: None formal: this step justifies a choice of setting rather than a claim.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepIV.content: To apply bi-coricity of units, one must use units vertically once-shifted, at (n,m−1), relative to the value group structures at (n,m) (Rem 3.11.3 (ii)). The conflict between needing a vertical shift and the impossibility of shifting (Step iii) is resolved by working on the 0-column with structures invariant under vertical shifts, namely vertically coric structures (n,◦), related to Frobenius-like structures by the log-Kummer correspondence of Thm 3.11 (ii), at the cost of the upper semi-compatibility Ind3.
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepIV.conclusion: Nature of the justification in the text: argument by reference.
obligations: Formalize the passage from Frobenius-like data at (0,0) to vertically coric data at (0,◦) and quantify the loss as a containment.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepV.content: Relate the units of the 0- and 1-columns by the unit portion 0,0 𝔉^{⊢×μ}_LGP ≅ 1,0 𝔉^{⊢×μ}_△ of the link and bi-coricity (Thm 1.5 (iii), (iv)); mono-analytic log-shells serve as multiradial mono-analytic containers for the local units, splitting monoids at V^bad and global Frobenioids indexed by (0,m), related to their (0,◦) versions by the log-Kummer correspondences of Thm 3.11 (ii) (a), (b), (c).
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepV.conclusion: Nature of the justification in the text: citation.
obligations: Show that the bi-coric log-shells at (0,◦) and (1,◦) are identified by the poly-isomorphisms, so that regions in one can be transported to the other.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepVI.content: The log-Kummer correspondences of Thm 3.11 (ii) (b), (c) come from splittings, up to roots of unity, into unit and value group portions via Galois evaluation (Rem 2.2.2 (iii), 2.3.2); the Kummer theory of LGP-monoids depends on IUTchII §3 and on [EtTh] (discrete rigidity, isomorphism class compatibility), and on conjugate synchronization from the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry, which is compatible with the log-link. Fig. 3.7 compares three approaches to cyclotomic rigidity (mono-theta environments, MLF-Galois pairs, number fields via Q_{>0} ∩ Ẑ^× = {1}); they are said to be mutually compatible '[one verifies immediately]'.
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepVI.conclusion: Nature of the justification in the text: assertion.
obligations: Prove mutual compatibility of the three cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms of Fig. 3.7.
ambiguities: 'one verifies immediately' with no argument.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepVII.content: Bi-coricity (Thm 1.5 (iii), (iv)) depends on conjugate synchronization from the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry, relating data at distinct labels in |F_l| compatibly with vertical coricity and Kummer theory while not identifying distinct labels; it is incompatible with the F^⊛_l-symmetry, so the two symmetries are treated separately; both are compatible with vertical coricity on the 0-column.
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepVII.conclusion: Nature of the justification in the text: citation.
obligations: Formalize conjugate synchronization and the F^{⋊±}_l- and F^⊛_l-symmetries (IUTchI, IUTchII vocabulary).

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepVIII.content: Constructing the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry uses global ±-synchronizations of local ±-indeterminacies; since local tempered fundamental groups at V^bad do not extend to a global one, these give profinite conjugacy indeterminacies in the vertically coric LGP-monoids, resolved by IUTchI §2.
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepVIII.conclusion: Nature of the justification in the text: citation.
obligations: Formalize ±-synchronization (IUTchI §2, Remark 6.12.4 (iii)).

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepIX.content: The copies of F_mod (global Frobenioids F_MOD, F_mod and realifications) bridge multiplicative global realified Frobenioids and their additive representations in mono-analytic log-shells; F_MOD is precisely compatible with the log-Kummer correspondence, hence suited to the link; F_mod is only upper semi-compatible (Ind3), hence suited to explicit degree estimates via log-volumes (Rem 3.10.1 (ii), (iii)).
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepIX.conclusion: Nature of the justification in the text: citation.
obligations: Formalize F_MOD and F_mod and prove the stated compatibility and semi-compatibility.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepX.content: Kummer-detachment gives Ind1 (permutation symmetries of the étale picture), Ind2 (automorphisms of the horizontal arrows) and Ind3 (vertical arrows). The procession-normalized log-volumes (average over j ∈ F*_l) are invariant under Ind1, Ind2 '[one verifies immediately, cf. Prop 3.9 (ii)]' and convert Ind3 into an inequality from above. log-link compatibility (Prop 3.9 (iv)) makes these log-volumes compatible with the arrows of the log-Kummer correspondence. Tensor products identify multiplication by integers, hence its effect on log-volumes, at different labels j ∈ F*_l.
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepX.conclusion: Nature of the justification in the text: assertion with citation.
obligations: Prove invariance of the averaged log-volume under each element of Ind1 (procession automorphisms) and each element of Ind2 (∏ Ism or ±1 on direct summands).
Prove that Ind3 containments give log-volume upper bounds (monotonicity of measure).
Prove that invariance holds for the joint action of Ind1 and Ind2 (generated group), not only for each separately.
ambiguities: Ind1 is defined (Thm 3.11 (i)) as automorphisms of the procession; Step (x) describes it as arising from permutation symmetries of the étale picture. The two descriptions are not shown to coincide.
Average index j ∈ F*_l here (page 181) versus |F_l| in (xi-d) (page 183).

source.pages_read: text; rendered and checked: pages 181 to 185

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.content: The comparison of the multiradial representation with the q-pilot object, divided into substeps (xi-a) to (xi-h).
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.conclusion: Nature of the justification in the text: see substeps.
obligations: See substep records.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXII.content: Global realified Frobenioids are needed: the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link preserves only isomorphism classes of objects of Frobenioids (Rem 3.6.2 (i)); with local Frobenioids one could not tell whether an object at v ∈ V^non corresponds to a submodule of the log-shell or to its p_v^N-multiple, because local objects admit endomorphisms that are not automorphisms, which would make a precise log-volume computation meaningless.
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXII.conclusion: Nature of the justification in the text: argument.
obligations: Prove that isomorphism classes of objects of the global realified Frobenioid determine the degree (log-volume), while those of local Frobenioids do not determine the p_v^N scaling.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.a.content: Consider a q-pilot object at (1,0) in terms of holomorphic log-shells at (1,0). The Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link (0,0) → (1,0) may be interpreted as a gluing isomorphism relating the holomorphic structures at (1,0) and (0,0) so that the Θ-pilot object at (0,0) corresponds to the q-pilot object at (1,0).
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.a.conclusion: Nature of the justification in the text: argument by definition.
obligations: Identify precisely which map the 'gluing isomorphism' is (the value group poly-isomorphism of Step (i)) and in which structure the correspondence Θ-pilot ↔ q-pilot holds (F^{⊩▶}-prime-strips only).

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.b.content: The multiradial construction algorithm of Thm 3.11 yields a collection of possibilities of output data in 0,◦U ≅ 1,◦U (the isomorphism from the permutation symmetries of Thm 3.11 (i)), satisfying IPL and SHE (Rem 3.11.1). The F^{⊩▶} portion of the link to the input data consists of full poly-isomorphisms of F^{⊩▶}-prime-strips; the F^{⊢×μ} portion is 'somewhat more complicated' because of Ind1, Ind2, Ind3. The algorithm is treated as 'some' algorithm with properties IPL and SHE, temporarily forgetting its internal structure (HIS).
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.b.conclusion: Nature of the justification in the text: assertion with citation.
obligations: State IPL as a precise property: each possible output is related to the input F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strip by an isomorphism of F^{⊩▶}-prime-strips.
State SHE precisely: the output is expressible in the arithmetic holomorphic structure of the 1-column.
Prove that the algorithm of Thm 3.11 satisfies both, jointly.
ambiguities: The precise relation 'somewhat more complicated' for the F^{⊢×μ} portion is not specified.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.c.content: Summary: the algorithm yields possibilities in 1,◦U ⊆ 1,◦U^Q linked (IPL) via isomorphisms of F^{⊩▶}-prime-strips to the representation, via the log-Kummer correspondence in the 1-column, of the q-pilot object at (1,0) on 1,◦U^Q, and expressible relative to the holomorphic structure in the 1-column (SHE). Passing to the hull 1,◦Ū ⊇ 1,◦U expresses the output in terms of localizations of arithmetic vector bundles over local rings O_{K_v}, which is necessary for comparability with the q-pilot object (an arithmetic line bundle).
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.c.conclusion: Nature of the justification in the text: argument.
obligations: Show the hull of a compact region is a free O_{K_v}-module of finite rank (a localization of an arithmetic vector bundle).

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.d.content: Taking the determinant (a suitable positive tensor power) of these vector bundle localizations and the suitably normalized (with respect to j ∈ |F_l|) log-volume of 1,◦Ū and of the region representing the q-pilot object yields comparable objects R_{≤−|log(Θ)|} = {λ ∈ R | λ ≤ −|log(Θ)|} and −|log(q)| ∈ R, where −|log(Θ)| is the (negative) log-volume of 1,◦Ū and −|log(q)| the log-volume of the q-pilot region on 1,◦U^Q. Global arithmetic degrees are log-volumes (Prop 3.9 (iii)). The log-Kummer correspondence in the 1-column rectifies the vertical shift between the unit portion of 1,0 𝔉_△^{⊩▶×μ} and the log-shells forming 1,◦U.
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.d.conclusion: Nature of the justification in the text: argument with citation.
obligations: Prove that the log-volume of the determinant (tensor power M) of the hull equals M times the normalized log-volume of the hull, so that M cancels.
Prove that the q-pilot region and the hull are measured by the same normalized log-volume (same index set for the average, same weights).
Prove that the log-Kummer correspondence identifies the unit portion at (1,0) with the log-shells at (1,◦) without changing log-volumes.
ambiguities: Normalization 'with respect to j ∈ |F_l|' (page 183) versus average over j ∈ F*_l (pages 173, 181).

The set R_{≤−|log(Θ)|} is introduced as 'possible log-volumes of pilot-object output data'; why every real number below −|log(Θ)| is a possible log-volume, rather than only the log-volumes of actual possible images, is not argued.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.e.content: The relationship between the pilot-object log-volume −|log(q)| and the input F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strip is the one imposed by the holomorphic structure in the 1-column. SHE amounts precisely to expressibility via operations that are well defined even under the condition that the pilot-object log-volume of the input data (linked via isomorphisms of F^{⊩▶}-prime-strips to the possible outputs) equals −|log(q)|. Hence the algorithm, with hull and log-volume, yields possible log-volumes R_{≤−|log(Θ)|} linked (IPL) to the pilot-object log-volume −|log(q)| of the input data (SHE).
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.e.conclusion: Nature of the justification in the text: argument by reformulation.
obligations: Formalize 'expressible under the condition that the input log-volume equals −|log(q)|' as a statement about the algorithm's domain of definition.
Prove that this condition is compatible with (does not alter) the output set R_{≤−|log(Θ)|}.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.f.content: The construction of R_{≤−|log(Θ)|} is subject to the condition that it constitutes a construction (perhaps only up to some sort of 'approximation', due to the indeterminacies) of the pilot-object log-volume −|log(q)| of the input data. The inclusion −|log(q)| ∈ R_{≤−|log(Θ)|}, hence −|log(q)| ≤ −|log(Θ)|, then follows formally.
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.f.conclusion: Nature of the justification in the text: assertion followed by a formal step.
obligations: Prove the inclusion −|log(q)| ∈ R_{≤−|log(Θ)|} from properties of the construction (this is the whole content; see docs/COR312_ANALYSIS.md).
The final passage from inclusion to inequality is checked in Lean as Iff.rfl: IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.stepXIf_inclusion_iff_inequality.
ambiguities: 'perhaps only up to some sort of approximation' (page 184) leaves the sense of 'construction of −|log(q)|' unspecified; the inclusion requires an exact statement.
Assessment: at the level of real numbers the premise of the last step is the conclusion; any non-circular argument must establish the inclusion at the level of regions or of the algorithm.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.g.content: Summary: the algorithm, followed by hull and log-volume, yields two tautologically equivalent ways to compute the log-volume of the q-pilot object at (1,0) (Fig. 3.8): via Kummer-detachment and the log-Kummer correspondence from the Θ-pilot at (0,0) compatibly with the link, then the permutation symmetry to (1,◦) and comparison via hull and log-volume; or directly from the q-pilot object at (1,0).
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.g.conclusion: Nature of the justification in the text: assertion.
obligations: Make 'tautologically equivalent' precise: state which two quantities are equal or which inequality holds between them.
ambiguities: The two computations yield −|log(Θ)| (an upper bound region) and −|log(q)| (a number); 'equivalent' cannot mean equality of these numbers, since the conclusion is an inequality.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.h.content: The argument depends essentially on [EtTh], which admits no evident generalization to N-th tensor powers of Θ-pilot objects for N ≥ 2: the log-volume of such a power must be computed as N times that of the original. The analogue for N-th powers would give sharper inequalities, which are false (IUTchIV Rem 2.3.2 (ii)).
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.h.conclusion: Nature of the justification in the text: assertion with citation.
obligations: Identify the step of (xi-a) to (xi-f) that fails for N-th powers, so that a formalization of the N = 1 argument visibly uses an N = 1 specific hypothesis.
ambiguities: The text does not point to which substep uses N = 1; the dependence on [EtTh] is stated but not located.

IUT3.Rem3_12_1.content: (i) IUTchIV seeks explicit upper bounds C_Θ. (ii) For λ ∈ Q_{>0}, generalized Θ^{×μ}_LGP-links q^λ ↦ q^{(1², ..., (l*)²)} give a similar theory, and 'one may apply the same arguments' to conclude C_Θ ≥ −λ; this is sharper for λ < 1 but irrelevant to IUTchIV, whose bounds are unaffected by a constant of absolute value ≤ 1. (iii) mono-theta cyclotomic rigidity as a 'canonical profinite volume' associated to the first power.
obligations: Check which steps of the proof change when the q-pilot is replaced by q^λ.
ambiguities: Assessment: (ii) asserts that the argument applies to q^λ for all λ ∈ Q_{>0}, while (xi-h) says the argument does not generalize to N-th powers on the theta side. The text distinguishes the two (power on the q side versus on the theta side); a formalization must check that the q-side generalization uses no step that (xi-h) excludes.
